lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1674: the dead life answers for itself

Item one of "fix all existing issues one through six": #110, the process kill
on nearly every boot. This is not the fix for the kill. It is the instrument
that the previous instrument turned out to be missing — and, by the owner's own
rule recorded in contextLedger.ts, that is the correct thing to ship: measure
the cause, or ship an instrument.

WHAT THE 19:40 LEDGER SAID, ENTRY BY ENTRY
Ten records. Eight at `stage boot:qwen:deferred`. Six of those dead 670–1006ms
into the process, `alive 0ms` after the stamp, `(no action yet)` — sub-second,
before the first screen, before Qwen has loaded (it is DEFERRED). And every one
of the eight: `not an OTA-apply boot`.

Three things ruled out before anything was written:
- a boot-front race — App.tsx AWAITS the OTA check and RETURNS on 'applied',
  so `qwen:deferred` is unreachable on an apply. My first hypothesis, and wrong;
- anything heavy at that stage — `armQwenWarm` stores a closure and returns;
- ML init — mlHealth reports crash count 0.

AND THE ONE THING THAT COULD NOT BE RULED EITHER WAY
OTA-1587 asked of every death: did the process that died boot on the far side
of `reloadAsync`? It stored the answer in the wrong life. The handoff that
carries it is consumed on read — correctly; a handoff is a fact about ONE boot
— by the life that then dies, taking the only copy with it. The next boot finds
no handoff, computes `afterOtaApply: false` about ITSELF, and bootSlice wrote
that onto the dead life's record. Structurally, a death record could never say
"yes". "Not an OTA-apply boot" on eight of ten was not a finding; it was the
only value the field could take. The ota1587 suite pinned the exact line —
`afterOtaApply: launch.afterOtaApply,` — as correct.

So the fact now rides the CRUMB. `bootStampFields()` (the one writer every
crumb passes through) adds `afterOta` / `otaPath` / `otaGapMs` / `prevCtx` once
`noteLaunchFacts` has run — early in hydrate, before any stage that matters —
and the record reads the dead life's own answer off its own crumb. A crumb from
the first milliseconds, before the launch resolved, leaves it UNDEFINED, and
every reader prints that as "not known", never as a cold start. "Not known" is
a fact; "false" is a lie, and it is exactly the lie that hid this for two OTAs.

TWO MORE THINGS THE SAME READ TURNED UP
- The ledger label keyed on `kind` alone, so the idle reclaims OTA-1567 already
  made non-fatal (`isFatal: false`, and Sentry has honoured that as level
  `error` since) still printed PROCESS KILLED — no JS ran in About and in every
  bug report, and were counted in "N recorded". Two of the owner's ten were
  that. A ledger that overstates kills to the one person reading it sends the
  hunt at the wrong thing — OTA-1521's own words. The label now says what the
  record knew, and the header says "10 recorded, 8 fatal".
- The whole `launch` block — which life died, how old it was, what it inherited
  — has been on every record since OTA-1587 and forwarded to Sentry on none.
  The rollup it exists for could only ever be done by hand, on a device. It is
  in `extra` now, three-valued.

The OTA-1587 rollup counts FATAL kills and only a true "yes"; an idle reclaim
on an apply boot is not the signal, and `undefined` is not a "no" — counting it
as one would be the same defect one layer down. It also says out loud how many
died before their launch resolved, because the absence of that line is how the
hole hid.

⚠ NO BOOT-PHASE EXEMPTION, DELIBERATELY. Six sub-second no-action deaths look
exactly like a force-close during the splash — the owner's recorded habit. They
also look exactly like OTA-1587's candidate (b): a reload-boot killed by a
native context the previous life never released, in a process `reloadAsync`
does not restart. This instrument is what tells those two apart. Filing them as
non-fatal today would hide (b) if it is real — the blind-spot trade OTA-1377 and
OTA-1413 both refused. The next log closes #110 one way or the other.

- app/diagnostics/bootIdentity.ts — `BootStamp`, `bootStampFields` carries the
  launch facts once resolved.
- app/engine/saveSystem.ts — `LiveBreadcrumb` gains the four fields.
- app/state/slices/bootSlice.ts — the record reads the crumb, not the reader.
- app/diagnostics/crashLedger.ts — `recordLabel`, `isFatalRecord`, the header,
  the rollup over fatal with `=== true` and the unresolved line, the three-way
  launch line, `launch.otaPath`.
- app/diagnostics/sentryTransport.ts — `launch*` in `extra`.
- __tests__/ota1674TheDeadLifeAnswers.test.ts — 19 tests.
- __tests__/ota1587WhichLifeDied.test.ts — the pin on the defect repointed to
  the fix, with the reason.
